title: Introduce Slot Rebalancer: drift-aware reallocation and soft-preempt safety
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: Dedicated fleet allocations can accumulate subtle slot-level drift when tenants scale independently and autoscalers reconfigure concurrently. Drift causes aggressive preemption and rebind churn during rebalancing windows, increasing tail latency and work lost to KV cache misses. This PR introduces a Slot Rebalancer controller that performs drift-aware reallocation with a configurable reallocation window and 'soft-preempt' handoff semantics. The goal is to smooth commit transfers across GPU slots, reduce eviction spikes, and preserve throughput guarantees during rolling rebalances. Key ideas: 1) periodic 'slot heat' sampling to estimate fractional utilization and drift; 2) compute minimal move set to satisfy proportional fairness while minimizing preemptions; 3) soft-preempt protocol: mark migrating slots with extended preemption grace, allow KV cache shadowing for a short tail, and coordinate with request router to drain in-flight tokens; 4) safety fences and abort thresholds to avoid unsafe oscillations. Changes include controller implementation, autoscaler policy hook, integration tests, canary rollout scaffolding, and new telemetry. Checklist: - [x] Design reviewed (ENG-8432) - [x] Core algorithm implemented with unit tests - [x] Integration tests for small/large cluster scenarios - [x] Canary feature flag + canary config (5% tenants) - [x] Telemetry and alert rules added - [x] Docs and operator runbook drafted How to test locally: run test/integration/rebalancer_test.go against a 3-node emulated fleet (scripts/test-fleet.sh); use --feature-flag=slot-rebalancer to toggle. Rollout plan: enable feature-flag in canary region (us-west2) for 5% tenants for 48 hours, monitor new metrics (slot_rebalancer_moves_total, slot_rebalance_abort_rate, slot_move_latency_seconds_p95), then ramp to 25% if stable, then full rollout. Fallback: revert flag (safe fast-path) or switch to legacy greedy allocator. Related: ENG-8520 integrates allocator policy hooks; follow-up to ENG-7991 (kv-cache shadowing).

release_notes: Introduce Slot Rebalancer controller to reduce preemption churn during fleet rebalances.
Add soft-preempt handoff to preserve KV cache warmth during slot migrations and reduce tail latency.
New telemetry: slot_rebalancer_moves_total, slot_move_latency_seconds_p95, slot_rebalance_abort_rate; operators should monitor abort rate during rollout.
test_plan: Unit tests cover algorithm invariants and tie-breaking; integration tests include small-cluster and large-cluster scenarios (3-node/15-node). Canary plan: enable feature-flag for 5% tenants in us-west2 for 48h, validate p95 generation latency and abort rate < 0.5%, then ramp to 25% and full rollout. Rollback: flip feature-flag or disable controller; legacy allocator remains available.
operational_runbook: docs/ops/dedicated-rebalancer.md contains operator steps: how to inspect slot_move_latency histogram, force aborts, scale controller replicas, and fallback to legacy allocator. Key alerts: slot_rebalance_abort_rate > 1% for 15m, slot_move_latency_seconds_p95 > 5s for 10m.
notes_for_oncall: During canary watch for spikes in request 99th percentile latency correlated with slot_move_timestamp in request traces.
If abort rate spikes, immediately set feature-flag to off and open incident; backport log bundle from staging and tag ENG-8432.
